text:
maria: Quick sync — legal pushed back on GA contracts asking for a clear mapping between customer tiers and SLAs. We need confirmed SLA language + who owns the doc pages + oncall commitments by EOD Friday. Anyone blocking?

alex: I can own the engineering bits (latency/capacity tradeoffs) but need clear SLO targets. Are customers expecting p99 latency SLOs or just uptime/availability?

kevin: Two upcoming enterprise customers asked for contractual language around both uptime (99.95%) and latency for their low-latency workloads. They specifically asked for p99 <= 300ms for inference (50-100 token avg). Not asking for SLA dollars yet but want it surfaced in contracts.

linh: 300ms p99 is tough at current quantization + batching defaults on some models. We can hit it on small models with dedicated pools but not across the hosted catalog. Need to enumerate which model families and deployment modes the SLA would apply to. Also we require a 72h burn-in window before contractual coverage, and a playbook for degraded nodes.

maria: Good — so items we need: (1) canonical SLA table mapping customer tier -> metrics (availability, p99 latency by model family, error budget) (2) doc pages for the SLA + limitations/footnotes (3) oncall/runbook addendum (what we will and won't remediate) (4) pricing/credits if SLA breached. Assign owners?

alex: I’ll produce a table with model families (redwood-7b, r-13b, open-l6) and our measured p50/p95/p99 under Dedicated vs Hosted by Wednesday. That will include recommended guardrails (max tokens, batch size).

sarah: I’ll coordinate the pricing/credits tiering with finance — need to know expected incident frequency to model expected payouts. If we expose granular SLA we should also expose higher-cost Dedicated tiers with stricter SLOs.

kevin: I’ll draft the contractual language and loop in legal once we have the metrics table. Also will confirm which customers actually require latency SLAs vs just uptime.

linh: For monitoring and oncall: we need these concrete items in the runbook:
- Metrics: request_rate, p50/p95/p99_latency, request_error_rate, model_fallback_rate, queue_time
- Alerts: p99 > target for >10min (warn), sustained >30min (pager)
- Escalation: Eng Platform -> SRE -> Product on-call -> Legal (for customer notices)

linh: Example alert snippet (prometheus alert syntax):
```
alert: InferenceP99High
expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_family)) > 0.3
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: warning
annotations:
  summary: "p99 latency high for {{ $labels.model_family }}"
```

maria: Nice. Also need docs ownership: I propose product maintains the SLA prose page + FAQ; eng owns the metric definitions page; SRE owns runbooks/alerts. Can we confirm?

alex: agreed — eng will own metric definitions and the 'how we measure' appendix. I’ll add a short section on sampling, KV cache warming, and how quantization changes p99.

kevin: Sales asks we include an exceptions section (e.g., third-party networking outages, customer-provided model hosting, force majeure) and the 72h burn-in window. Legal will expect that.

maria: Action items summary (owners):
- SLA mapping table (alex) — due Wed COB
- SLA prose + FAQ (maria) — draft Thu AM
- Runbook + alerts (linh) — initial version Thu COB
- Pricing/credits model (sarah) — draft Fri AM
- Contract language + exceptions (kevin -> legal) — Fri EOD

deploy-bot: Reminder: engineering metrics job scheduled for 1767774350 to run p99 profiling across dedicated pools.

maria: One more ask — we must be explicit in docs about scope: which deployment modes (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) the SLA applies to and whether quantized/experimental runtimes are excluded. Avoid blanket promises.

linh: Agreed. Also recommend a fallback policy: if primary model family can't meet p99 for X% of requests, we automatically route to a verified lower-latency variant and notify customer. Need product signoff on automatic fallback being allowed in contracts.

maria: OK — noting that as a decision to capture. If nobody objects I’ll consolidate these action items and owners into a short PR today and tag legal + oncall.

alex: thumbs up from platform.

kevin: +1 from sales. I’ll start drafting client-facing phrasing.

linh: will flesh runbook and alerts, and attach test results from the profiling job when ready.

maria: Thanks — I’ll create the PR and assign reviewers: @alex, @linh, @sarah, @kevin. We’ll reconvene Fri 10am if any open items.
